messages:
jordan: Quick RFC follow-up re: canary / A-B rollouts + automatic fallback. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and a proposed starter architecture before we lock design. Thoughts?

anya: +1. Can we make sure we cover per-tenant vs global rollouts and how KV cache / session state behaves on fallback?

leo: For starters I think we should separate two concerns: (1) traffic routing + rollout controller, (2) health evaluation + fallback trigger. Keep controller stateless.

kevin: Agree. Controller = config + assignment store. Health evaluator = streaming metrics consumer that emits flags. That way fallback decisions can be local to runtime or centralized.

jordan: Tradeoffs: centralized evaluator -> single source of truth, easier global metrics, but adds a control-plane dependency on low-latency decisions. Local evaluator -> faster failover, more variance across zones. Which is our priority?

ria: We should optimize for safety first: automatic fallback must never increase P99 latency or cause incorrect responses. I'd prefer conservative local fast-fallback for safety, with central rollup for visibility.

leo: Implementation sketch: rollout-controller (control plane) stores rollout configs: percentage, cohorts, model-variants, match rules, TTLs. Runtimes poll or subscribe to assignments and apply them. Health-evaluator runs both centrally (for analytics) and locally (for fast triggers) using same rules and thresholds.

anya: Important: per-request vs per-session fallback. If a canary fails once, do we route the entire session back to baseline? I think session affinity should be preserved for chat state (KV cache coherence).

kevin: Yeah. Suggestion: three fallback scopes: request-level (for transient errors), session-level (sticky for chat / KV coherence), and tenant-level (for long-lived rollbacks). Configurable in rollout manifest.

jordan: What metrics to use for auto-fallback? error-rate, token-generation-exceptions, abnormal latency spike, quality regression (evals), and an anomaly on semantic drift (if available). Keep thresholds conservative: e.g., error-rate > 1% for 5min or P95 latency +50%.
messages_continued:
deploy-bot: [deploy] canary deploy started for model: open-llama-13b-q4a variant=fast-quant; rollout=5% -> 10% over 30m window :rocket:

leo: Also need to emit a 'fallback reason' tag in logs so Console can attribute root cause (e.g., kernel OOM, kv-cache-miss cascade, model-evaluation-fail). This helps prevent oscillation where controller flips back and forth.

ria: Oscillation prevention: introduce cooldown windows and exponential backoff for re-try, plus require stabilizing window before increasing traffic again. Also support manual override in Console.

anya: KV cache: when routing a session from canary -> baseline, we need to either: (a) rehydrate baseline cache from session prefix (if compatible), (b) bust cache and accept cold-start penalty, or (c) keep using canary only for reads while writes go to baseline (risky). We should document that model-variant compatibility is a hard constraint for sticky routing or else session fallback = cache bust.

leo: Agreed. Early-stage rule: only allow session-affinity rollouts between model-variants with same tokenizer + compatible KV layout. Otherwise disallow session stickiness in the config and fall back at request-level only.

kevin: Integration with routing runtime: runtime implements a simple policy chain: 1) check assignment table -> route target, 2) consult local health flags -> override to fallback if necessary, 3) apply per-session affinity rules, 4) call model. Fallback events are emitted to control-plane with sampling.

jordan: Failure modes: (1) control-plane unavailable -> runtimes should continue last-known assignment (graceful degradation), (2) metric lag causes false negatives -> local short-term thresholds, (3) mass fallback -> capacity pressure on baseline -> circuit-breaker to limit fallback rate.

ria: Good call on circuit-breaker. We should also rate-limit automatic fallback so it doesn't send 100% traffic to baseline in <1s; use a ramping throttle.

anya: A/B experiments: Controller should record cohort membership and attach experiment ids to logs. Post-hoc analysis needs stable sampling keys (tenant id, request hash) to correlate quality signals. Store these in request headers so downstream evaluators can compute metrics.

leo: Config example (rollout manifest):
```yaml
rollout_id: r-2026-03-canary1
percent: 5
cohorts: [random(tenant_hash, seed=42)]
scope: session
compatible_variants: [open-llama-13b-q4a, open-llama-13b-q4b]
fallback_policy:
  criteria:
    error_rate: {threshold: 0.01, window: 300}
    p95_latency: {threshold_pct: 150, window: 300}
  scope_override: request
  cooldown: 600
```

kevin: Nice. For rollout storage use existing config-store (etcd) and expose REST + websocket subscription for low-latency updates. Runtimes should apply rollouts in-memory and persist last-known assignment to disk for restarts.

jordan: Long-term refactor proposal: extract rollout-controller as dedicated microservice with an SDK for runtimes. Integrate with Console to allow safe canary creation and visual rollback. Provide an API to plug-in alternate health evaluators (ML quality service).

ria: Also add a 'simulator' in Console that can run rollouts against historical traces to estimate error-rate/latency impact before live rollout. Low effort, high value.

anya: One more: telemetry. Emit an event stream for every fallback with fields: rollout_id, tenant_id, session_id, fallback_scope, reason, pre_target, post_target. Keep sampling low but full for incidents.

leo: Open question: automated quality fallback (using evals). We can tie continuous eval pipelines: if canary fails quality checks vs baseline on a canned prompt set, then schedule automatic rollback. But beware small sample sizes early in rollout. Use Bayesian priors.

jordan: Next steps: 1) I'll draft a short RFC capturing controller/evaluator split + manifest schema, 2) leo/kevin to prototype runtime hooks and websocket subscription, 3) ria/anya to define fallback metrics + cooldown defaults, 4) ops to add circuit-breaker defaults. We'll sync Tues 10am.

kevin: I'm fine to pair on prototyping.

ria: Thanks — pushing for the simulator too. :+1:

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary rollback triggered for r-2026-03-canary1 reason=error_rate_threshold, traffic_reverted=5% -> 0%

jordan: Nice test. Let's capture pain points during the prototype and iterate.

kevin: One minor UX ask: add 'simulate fallback' button in Console so PMs can see what would have happened for given window.

anya: Also document how to write rollout manifests and compatibility matrix for model variants. I'll start a docs draft.

leo: Will sketch the architecture diagram and wireframes for SDK surface.

jordan: Thanks team — I'll drop the RFC + action items in the thread.
